title: India Semiconductor Mission
summary: India's subsidy programme to build domestic chip packaging and fabrication.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

The India Semiconductor Mission, launched in 2021 with about US$10bn of incentives, has approved assembly and test plants and a fabrication project, with Micron's Sanand facility and Tata's Dholera fab among the anchors. The strategy starts with packaging, which is capital-light relative to leading-edge fabs, and hopes to move up. Execution depends on water, power and skilled labour.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Pilot
Estimated window 2021–2030
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Packaging is the realistic entry point for new geographies; it builds skills before capital-intensive fabs.

What Would Change The View

  • Plant commissioning and customer qualification.
  • Fab construction progress.
  • Workforce training pipeline.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
